proof.criterion: R7's malformed-value branch, which review round 2 corrected: a value this build cannot decode names no instance and is deleted, wherever the type error sits. No HTTP client can reach this branch, since only a client of the bucket can store such a value.
proof.surface: The envoy_sessions KV bucket itself, written with the nats client from a Bun driver, against a listener and nats-server built from this checkout; the deletes then go through the listener's real DELETE /v1/sessions/<id> route. This is the only surface that reaches the branch, and the correction it tests is exactly that Go's json.Unmarshal fills every field it could read before a type error, so a malformed value carrying another instance's id would otherwise be compared against that id and kept.
proof.command: cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && bash /legion/scratch/tester/malformed.sh  (9 assertions; a scratch rig, kept out of the tree)
proof.observed: MALFORMED RESULT: 9 passed, 0 failed, and the listener logged its 'deleting a malformed value for a named client instance' warning 3 times. A value whose type error follows the id, one whose type error precedes it, and one that is not JSON at all were each answered {"deleted":true} by a request naming a different instance, and each was gone from the bucket afterwards; a malformed value is still deleted by a request naming no instance.
proof.negativeControl: The run's first two assertions are the control, and they are the case this branch must not swallow: a well-formed entry carrying another instance's id, deleted by a different instance, answered {"deleted":false,"reason":"the registration belongs to another client instance"} and stayed in the bucket. Without it a probe that deleted everything would read as a pass.

ciAtHead: CI run 41188502240 at the code head fcf43506541c (github.com/sjawhar/legion/actions/runs/41188502240), read at 09:35Z: one job, `changes`, still queued 12 minutes after the run was created, and no other lane started. Every earlier run on this branch — 41186682096, 41184223344, 41178943353, 41174385912 — is `cancelled`, each superseded by the next push's concurrency group. So after five heads no full lane set has settled on this pull request at any of them. That is the repository's runner backlog, not a verdict on the change, and it is a standing risk to the merge rather than to this phase: the base's required checks decide whether the merge happens, and none has yet run to completion here. I read a queued lane as queued, waited for none and re-ran none. The pull-request head 32b149cd is the handoff-only commit and carries the skip-checks trailer, so GitHub started nothing for it.
observations: The Go change since the head I tested in round 2 is a comment alone (packages/envoy/internal/session/registry.go, the decode comment's wording), which I diffed rather than assumed, so the listener binary decides what it decided last round. I re-ran every listener probe anyway and each answered identically.

This round's one unreachable change is the parameterised warning: handle.unregisterTopics now carries the caller's sentence (envoy.ts:2254 hands it 'envoy: could not unregister a resumed controller's retired Slack topics'). Its one caller is the controller's Slack retirement on resume, and the warning appears only when that unsubscribe fails, which I cannot provoke from outside. It is covered by the module's own tests (registration-state.test.ts:556, :571, :579). Recorded so nobody reads it as covered by a live run.

The other plugin change is inert by construction: claimRole's two refusal messages at :612 and :637 were unread, because run() swallows a StepRefused message, and the sentence the model reads is chosen at envoy.ts:2033-2035 from claimAdopted. Removing them cannot change what a caller hears, and the role-takeover smoke drives that refusal path three times in row 5.

poll_until (local-stack.sh:57-65) is the same budget as the two loops it replaced in the stall smoke — 30 s for natsd and 60 s for the listener — measured in wall-clock seconds with a final check, rather than in iterations that ignored the time each probe took, so it is if anything the stricter of the two. Both arms then passed on it.

A note on my own rig, so a later reader does not mistake it for a product fault: six concurrent copies of my probe script share one work directory and so delete each other's NATS store, which produced one failing run in six. Every sequential run is 37 of 37. While chasing that I also found that the listener's /healthz turns green before its /v1 routes open — the starting gate's own 503, {"error":"service starting"}, which api.go distinguishes from the bus-unavailable 503 on purpose — so my rigs now wait on GET /v1/sessions. That is the listener behaving as documented, not a defect, but it is worth knowing for anyone writing a readiness wait against it.
